title: Localization embeds into generic fibre localizations
statement: Let $R\to B$ be a flat homomorphism of commutative rings of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map, def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Suppose $B\otimes_R K$ is a domain for every prime $\mathfrak p\subset R$ and field extension $K/\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-residue-field]. Let $\mathfrak q_{\mathfrak p}$ be the inverse image of the zero prime of $B\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. With spectra and localization as in [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-pbc-module-localization], the natural map $$B\longrightarrow\prod_{\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}R}B_{\mathfrak q_{\mathfrak p}}$$ is injective.

source.place: Tag 0810, final paragraph, generic-fibre localization injection; using Tag 05DH, lemma-base-change-universally-flat, after localization of the base.

proof.text: Fix $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}R$, put $A=R_{\mathfrak p}$, $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak pA$, $C=(R\setminus\mathfrak p)^{-1}B$, and $F=B\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. By [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], $A$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ and $C/\mathfrak mC=F$. By hypothesis $F$ is a nonzero domain. The map from the field $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ into $F$ is injective: its kernel is an ideal of a field and cannot contain $1$. Thus the inverse image $\mathfrak q=\ker(B\to F)$ is a prime with contraction $\mathfrak p$. Every element of $R\setminus\mathfrak p$ therefore becomes a unit in $D=B_{\mathfrak q}$, giving the canonical map $u:C\to D$.

source.place: Tag 0810, lemma-helper-blowup-affine-space, final paragraph; notation for the base-localized map in the displayed product injection

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-affine-geometrically-integral-projective] to the given $R\to B$. Its hypotheses are exactly the flatness, finite presentation and all-field-extension domain hypotheses of the item. Consequently choose a free $R$-module $E=\bigoplus_{i\in I}R$ and maps $j:B\to E$, $s:E\to B$ with $sj=1$, using [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. Localize these maps at $R\setminus\mathfrak p$; the fraction formulas preserve $sj=1$. The localized free module is $\bigoplus_{i\in I}A$: the isomorphism sends $(r_i)/t$ to $(r_i/t)$, and its inverse uses the product of the denominators of the finitely many nonzero coordinates. Hence $C$ is a direct summand of a free $A$-module, and is projective over $A$ by the same definition.

source.place: Tag 05FT, lemma-fibres-irreducible-flat-projective-nonnoetherian; projectivity input for the Tag 05FQ specialization of the Tag 0810 local injection

proof.text: The $A$-module $D$ is flat. Indeed, for an injection of $A$-modules $L_1\to L_2$, regard it as an injection of $R$-modules and tensor with the flat $R$-module $B$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Localizing this injection of $B$-modules at $T=B\setminus\mathfrak q$ is still injective: if $x/t$ maps to zero, some $v\in T$ kills its image numerator, so injectivity before localization gives $vx=0$ and $x/t=0$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. Identify $T^{-1}(L_i\otimes_R B)$ with $L_i\otimes_A D$ by $(l\otimes b)/t\mapsto l\otimes(b/t)$, with inverse $l\otimes(b/t)\mapsto(l\otimes b)/t$. Balancing over $A$ follows because each $r\notin\mathfrak p$ acts invertibly on $L_i$, with $r^{-1}l\otimes b=l\otimes(b/r)$ in the localized tensor product. The maps are inverse on generators [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. The resulting injection is exactly the tensor of $L_1\to L_2$ with $D$, proving the claim.

source.place: Tag 0810, final paragraph, flat localization at the fibre-generic prime; elementary tensor-and-fraction verification of the target-flatness hypothesis of Tag 05FQ

proof.text: The reduction of $u$ modulo $\mathfrak m$ is injective. In fact $D/\mathfrak mD$ is the localization of $F=C/\mathfrak mC$ at the images of $B\setminus\mathfrak q$. The identification sends the class of $b/t$ to $\bar b/\bar t$; its inverse sends $\bar c/\bar t$, with $c=b/r\in C$, to the class of $b/(rt)$. Changing $c$ by an element of $\mathfrak mC$ changes this fraction by an element of $\mathfrak mD$, and clearing denominators verifies both inverse equations [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime, def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. Every such $\bar t$ is nonzero by the definition of $\mathfrak q$. Thus $F\to D/\mathfrak mD$ is injective: $\bar b/1=0$ means $\bar t\bar b=0$ for one nonzero $\bar t$ in the domain $F$, whence $\bar b=0$. This is the actual reduction map of $u$, not an arbitrary injection of the two rings.

source.place: Tag 0810, final paragraph; verification of the residue injection needed for Tag 05FQ, lemma-universally-injective-local

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-local-universal-injective-residue] to $u:C\to D$ over the local ring $(A,\mathfrak m)$. Step 2 gives its projective source, step 3 its flat target, and step 4 its injective reduction. The criterion makes $u$ universally injective. Taking the tensor test module to be $A$ and identifying $A\otimes_A C=C$, $A\otimes_A D=D$ gives that $C\to D$ itself is injective. This proves the local inclusion used in the final paragraph of the source without introducing another node for that inclusion.

source.place: Tag 05FQ, lemma-universally-injective-local, applied to the local inclusion in Tag 0810; this supplies its needed special case of Tag 05DH

proof.text:
Let $b\in B$ map to zero in every $B_{\mathfrak q_{\mathfrak p}}$. Step 5 shows that $b/1=0$ in $(R\setminus\mathfrak p)^{-1}B$ for every prime $\mathfrak p\subset R$. If $b
e0$, its $R$-annihilator $J=\{r\in R:rb=0\}$ is proper, since $1
otin J$. By [lem-weil-pbc-proper-ideal-contained-in-maximal] choose a maximal ideal $\mathfrak p$ containing $J$; it is a prime. The fraction criterion [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] applied to $b/1=0$ supplies $r
otin\mathfrak p$ with $rb=0$. This puts $r\in J\subseteq\mathfrak p$, a contradiction. Hence $b=0$. The kernel of the displayed product homomorphism is zero, which proves its injectivity (apply the zero-kernel assertion to the difference of two elements with equal images). If $R$ is the zero ring then so is its unital algebra $B$ and the empty-product map is injective as well.

split_report.summary: Six-step proof of the fibre-generic product injection. Reuses the existing algebra-projectivity and local residue-injectivity criteria, with explicit localized splitting, flatness, residue-localization and annihilator arguments. No new nodes, no statement change, no Lean work.
split_report.blueprint: Preserves the full via chain from the local-term-locality semistable-alteration branch; realizes the final localization-injectivity paragraph of Tag 0810 in the affine flattening helper. Whole-blueprint searches found no equivalent statement.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q84-ebd7fba04 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the full item, all six steps and every cited statement, and checked them against Stacks flat.tex: Tag 0810 (lemma-helper-blowup-affine-space, final paragraph, the product inclusion S'_a ⊂ ∏ S'_q'' attributed to 05DH) and Tags 05DH (l.1907), 05FQ (l.1946) and 05FT (l.2247). The statement is unchanged and is not weaker than the source. The inverse image of the zero prime of the fibre equals pB, because B/pB is flat over R/p and so torsion-free. Step 1: the fibre ring is a nonzero domain, so q is a prime with contraction p and the map C→D exists. Step 2: the hypotheses of lem-trf-affine-geometrically-integral-projective (05FT) are exactly the item's, and the localized split gives C projective over A = R_p. Step 3: the flatness of D over A via T^{-1}(L⊗_R B) ≅ L⊗_A D checks out and is routine, so marking it elementary is acceptable. Step 4: the reduction map is F → F localized at nonzero elements of a domain, hence injective, with explicit inverses. Step 5: lem-trf-local-universal-injective-residue (05FQ) is used by its statement only, and taking L=A gives C→D injective. Step 6: the annihilator/maximal-ideal argument is correct, and R=0 is covered. proof_deps equals the union of uses. Both theorem inputs are unsplit nodes of the same unit sk-i-curve-zero with no dependency on the item, so there is no cycle and no off-route tool. No SGA source is used. Small cases tested: k[x]/k, Z[x]/Z, R[x] over R=k[ε]/ε² (nilpotents kept), a product of two fields, and R=0. The rg search over the DAG found no duplicate of the item. The worker's report that lem-trf-local-fibres-integral-projective duplicates lem-trf-affine-geometrically-integral-projective (05FT) is correct; that is a maintenance merge outside this delivery. There are no new nodes, no fixes and no tool_uses.
